The request

“The Level 4 meeting rooms are getting too warm in the afternoons. Can someone please look at the air conditioning?”

The turn

Four people did their job correctly and the job still took three and a half days.

Nobody was slow. They were each holding a different piece of the same request, and no system was holding all four at once. That gap is not a people problem. It is the only part of this worth automating.

38% of requests need at least one round of clarification before anyone can be dispatched.
17% are the same job, reported twice, through two different channels.

Where we stop

Facilities teams aren’t fired for being slow.

They’re fired for a job that went wrong. Readyset prepares decisions. It never makes them.

01

Your system stays the record

We write into it. We never become it. Turn us off tomorrow and you lose nothing.

02

Emergencies never touch us

Anything urgent or safety-related goes straight to your existing human pathway, unprocessed.

03

Duplicates are suggested, never merged

Best-in-class detection is right about 63% of the time. A wrong merge puts two tenants in one thread.

04

No trade or safety call is automated

We identify the asset and the access window. What’s wrong with it stays an authorised human judgement.

05

Every field shows its source

Tenant-stated, register-matched or coordinator-entered. The record stands up in a dispute.

06

Nobody installs anything

Emily keeps emailing. Marco keeps using simPRO. One forwarding rule is the whole integration.

Built in five hours

What’s real, and what’s staged.

Real

  • Field extraction from raw inbound maintenance email
  • Gap detection against a required-field set
  • The generated clarification question
  • Emergency routing check
  • Provenance stamped on every extracted field

Simulated

  • Asset register and floor-plate matching — fixture data
  • Write-back into a work-order system — mocked endpoint
  • Duplicate detection — rules on a seeded set, not a trained model
  • Emily, Leo, Marco and Aisha are from the scenario pack
  • Missed-appointment data is UK social housing, not Australian
